activityGoals.name: Modifying an Array (Case 1)
activityGoals.goalDescription: Construct a program that increments all elements of the array by 1.

commentList: We initialize the array of type int to hold the specified numbers. We initialize the array by separating elements with a comma and enclosing the collection in braces { }.

We want to iterate over the array and increment each element in the array by 1. To really change the array as we march across it, we need to use indexes so we can assign an updated value to each position as we go. We need the array indexes to start at 0 (array indexes start from 0) with every integer number up to but not including the array length.

Note that we cannot try changing array elements with for-each statement "for (x : lst)" that assigns the name x to each of the items in the array in turn, from left to right. Because updating variable x does not update the array where variable x originally came from; in this case, variable x is a piece of memory separate from the array.

In the first part of the loop header, we define a control variable i and initialize it to 0. In the second part of the loop header, we test whether the control variable has reached the termination threshold. The loop is repeated if the control variable is less than the number of the elements in the array and terminates when the control variable reaches the array length. In the third part of the loop header, we increment the control variable by 1 after each iteration of the loop.
We can get the number of elements in the array by using the lst.length expression.

Note that the first part is executed once before the loop starts, the second part is executed before each iteration, and the third part is executed after each iteration of the loop. Also note that the increment operator (++) adds 1 to the value of variable i and the result is stored back into the variable i. Therefore, it is functionally equivalent to the statement i = i + 1.

lineList.content: //Step 2.1: Increment the element at index i by 1

commentList: This statement increments the element at the index i of the array by 1.

The += operator adds 1 to the value of the index i in the array and the result is stored back into the index i of the array. Therefore, it is functionally equivalent to the statement lst[i] = lst[i] + 1.

To print the array elements, we need to traverse the array and then print each element as we visit it. We traverse the array elements using for–each statement. This for loop assigns the name x to each of the elements in the array in turn, from left to right, and the print statement will be executed for each.
This statement prints the element that we visited in the array followed by a space character.

Note that we don't use println because it adds an end-of-line character to terminate the output line. We want to print all the elements of the array in the same line; therefore, we use the print method.

activityGoals.name: Modifying an Array (Case 2)
activityGoals.goalDescription: Construct a program that swaps pairs of adjacent elements of the array. For example, if the array is {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}, the program will change it to {2, 1, 4, 3, 6, 5}.\nThis program assumes that the array has always an even number of elements.

commentList: We initialize the array of type int to hold the specified numbers. We initialize the array by separating elements with a comma and enclosing the collection in braces { }.

lineList.content: //Step 2: Iterate through the pairs of adjacent elements in the array

commentList: We want to iterate over the array and swap adjacent elements in the array. To really change the array as we march across it, we need to use indexes so we can assign an updated value to each position as we go. We need the array indexes to start at 0 (array indexes start from 0) with every second integer number up to but not including the array length.

Note that we cannot try changing array elements with for–each statement "for (x : lst)" that assigns the name x to each of the items in the array in turn, from left to right. Because first updating variable x does not update the array where variable x originally came from; in this case, variable x is a piece of memory separate from the array. Second, we need to access adjacent elements and we can get that only when iterate over the array indexes.

In the first part of the loop header, we define a control variable i and initialize it to 0. In the second part of the loop header, we test whether the control variable has reached the termination threshold. The loop is repeated if the control variable is less than the number of the elements in the array and terminates when the control variable reaches the array length. In the third part of the loop header, we increment the control variable by 2 after each iteration of the loop (because in each iteration we process the elements in index i and index i+1).
Note that the first part is executed once before the loop starts, the second part is executed before each iteration, and the third part is executed after each iteration of the loop.
We can get the number of elements in the array by using the lst.length expression.

Note that the += operator adds the value on the the right-hand side of the assignment operator (i.e., 2) to the current value of the variable on the left-hand side (i.e., value of variable i) and that value is stored in the variable i. Thus, this statement is equivalent to the statement i = i + 2.

lineList.content: //Step 2.1: Swap the element at index i with the element at index i+1

commentList: This statement stores the value of the element at index i of the array in the temporary variable temp. Later, we use variable temp to copy the content of the element at index i into the element at the index i+1.
This statement copies the value of the element at index i+1 of the array into the element at the index i of the array.
This statement copies the value of the element at index i that we stored in temporary variable temp into the element at index i+1 of the array.

This for loop assigns the name x to each of the elements in the array in turn, from left to right, and the print statement will be executed for each.
This statement prints the element that we visited in the array followed by a space character.

Note that we don't use println because it adds an end-of-line character to terminate the output line. We want to print all the elements of the array in the same line; therefore, we use the print method.
